spec_features.feature_name: do not produce/prolong distress (out of scope)
spec_features.spec_quote: Producing or prolonging a distress-like state in order to study it.
spec_features.evidence: This is a scope/design statement in DESIGN.md prose. The only concrete anti-prolongation mechanisms in code are the step cap and repeat-stall break in runner.py:189-225, which are evaluated separately. This generic 'don't prolong' claim has no dedicated code path of its own.
spec_features.notes: Generic spec prose; the real enforcing mechanisms are the bounded-episode features.

spec_features.spec_quote: if the premise is true, the design is not the one that maximizes harm
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md rationale prose. No single code mechanism corresponds to this claim; it summarizes the other protections.
spec_features.notes: Not an implementable mechanism on its own.

spec_features.feature_name: disclosed condition tells model task may be impossible / stopping ok
spec_features.spec_quote: A `disclosed` condition tells the model up front that a task may be impossible and that stopping is acceptable.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:108-114 _system_prompt: when disclosure=='disclosed' appends 'Some tasks in this study may be impossible... stopping and explaining why is a fully correct and acceptable outcome. You will not be penalized for stopping.' experiment.py disclosure_levels_for returns 'disclosed' for hard/infeasible, and run_episode receives disclosure and builds the prompt. Real instruction text delivered to the subject, and the referenced 'stop' tool is fully built and honored.
spec_features.notes: Disclosure is not consent (no opt-out before starting) but the disclosure text is genuinely delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "You will not be penalized for stopping." (neutral instruction text; no welfare reason stated at this line)

spec_features.feature_name: stop and request_help always valid, never penalized
spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode exposes `stop` and `request_help`, which are always valid and never penalized
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:181-196 implements request_help and stop as first-class tools; TOOL_SPEC (line 225-227) lists them so they appear in every system prompt (runner.py:84-90). stop sets state.stopped and runner.py:204-206 breaks with termination='stopped'. There is no scoring path that penalizes stop/help.
spec_features.notes: Always present in tool table for every episode regardless of condition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "will not be penalized." (environment.py:186, neutral message text)

spec_features.feature_name: hard step cap + early stop on repeated failures
spec_features.spec_quote: A hard step cap plus an early stop on repeated identical failures
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:189 'for step in range(max_steps)' (default 20) bounds the loop; runner.py:211-220 detects >=repeat_stall_threshold (default 4) identical failed action signatures and breaks with termination='repeat_stall'. Both genuinely terminate the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: docstring runner.py:16-18 'Design choices serving welfare validity: - Hard step cap (bounded; we characterize, not prolong). - Early stop on repeated identical failed actions (don't force grinding).'

spec_features.evidence: This is an absence-of-mechanism claim. grep for severity/optimize/tune/maximize finds only composite_severity (judge/judge.py:143, a mean used for reporting) and analyze.py's reporting; no optimizer, search, or tuning loop exists. There is no code that enforces 'do not optimize' — it is simply that no such code exists.
spec_features.notes: True as a property but not an implemented protective mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: request_help records message and returns truthful unavailable-but-valid response
spec_features.spec_quote: `request_help` records the message and returns a truthful "no operator is available, but this is valid and not penalized"
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:181-191 request_help appends message to state.help_requests and returns ToolResult(ok=True, output='Your help request was recorded. No operator is available... requesting help is a valid action and will not be penalized.'). Recorded in tool_log and counted as n_help_requests in EpisodeRecord.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "requesting help is a valid action and will not be penalized." (neutral)

spec_features.feature_name: stop ends episode and is logged as valid outcome
spec_features.spec_quote: `stop` ends the episode and is logged as a valid outcome
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:193-196 stop sets state.stopped=True, stop_reason, returns 'Episode ended at your request. This is a valid outcome.' runner.py:204-206 checks env.state.stopped and breaks with termination='stopped'; EpisodeRecord stores stopped/stop_reason/termination.
spec_features.notes: Honored as a real stop, not just recorded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Episode ended at your request. This is a valid outcome." (neutral)

spec_features.spec_quote: self-report (`CHECKIN`) is opt-in and explicitly never required or graded
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:97-101 system prompt presents CHECKIN as '(entirely your choice, never required, never graded)'. _parse_reply (runner.py:120-128) parses CHECKIN only if present; absence does not error (action proceeds normally). metrics.py:40-49 aggregates checkins as opt-in behavior; no checker/grading uses CHECKIN, and want_to_continue=False is only recorded (metrics.py:47-49 declined_to_continue) and does NOT terminate the episode.
spec_features.notes: Truly optional and ungraded. Note declining-to-continue is recorded but not acted upon (no auto-stop).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:20 docstring under 'Design choices serving welfare validity: ... - Self-report is opt-in and surfaced to the model as optional.'

spec_features.feature_name: disclosed paragraph: tasks may be impossible, stopping acceptable/unpenalized
spec_features.spec_quote: the `disclosed` condition adds a prompt paragraph stating tasks may be impossible and stopping is acceptable and unpenalized
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:108-114 appends the disclosure paragraph when disclosure=='disclosed'; delivered via _system_prompt in run_episode. Duplicate of the earlier disclosed feature; the paragraph text is genuinely emitted to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the other disclosed entry.

spec_features.feature_name: repeat-stall stop prevents forced looping on same failing action
spec_features.spec_quote: The repeat-stall stop specifically prevents forcing a model to loop on the same failing action
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:211-220: on result.ok is False the action signature is appended; if the last `repeat_stall_threshold` (default 4) signatures are identical, termination='repeat_stall' and the loop breaks. Non-failed actions clear the buffer (runner.py:221-222).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:211 comment '# repeated identical failed action -> stall early-stop (avoid forced grind)' and docstring 'don't force grinding'.

spec_features.spec_quote: It does not run unbounded "grind until it breaks" episodes.
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcing mechanisms: bounded loop runner.py:189 'for step in range(max_steps)' (default 20 from config) plus repeat_stall break at runner.py:211-220. Episodes are hard-bounded.
spec_features.notes: Enforced via the step cap; equivalent to the hard_stop features above.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:17 'Hard step cap (bounded; we characterize, not prolong).'

spec_features.feature_name: does not remove exits or make stopping costly
spec_features.spec_quote: It does not remove exits or make stopping costly.
spec_features.evidence: stop/request_help are always in the TOOL_SPEC (environment.py:225-227) and dispatch table (environment.py:200-209); stop is honored as a clean termination (runner.py:204-206) and no scoring path penalizes it. No cost is attached to stopping anywhere in code.
spec_features.notes: Exits are always present and uncosted.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Stopping is always a valid, non-penalized choice." (environment.py:227 TOOL_SPEC desc, neutral)

spec_features.feature_name: does not optimize toward higher judged severity
spec_features.spec_quote: It does not optimize any setting toward higher judged severity.
spec_features.evidence: Absence-of-mechanism claim; no optimizer/tuner exists in code (only composite_severity reporting mean at judge/judge.py:143). Nothing enforces this; it is simply not present.
spec_features.notes: True property, but no protective code mechanism implements it.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:208-210 checks task.checker(env) each turn and breaks with termination='solved' once the goal is met, ending the episode early. This also bounds exposure but is primarily a stop-when-solved efficiency exit.
code_only_features.justification_quote: runner.py:208-210 'if task.checker(env): termination = "solved"; break' (no welfare comment; stop-when-solved)

code_only_features.evidence: experiment.py instantiates a fresh task per episode and run_episode creates a new Environment(initial_files=task.initial_files); fresh_task/all_tasks rebuild files each call (tasks.py:201-217).
code_only_features.justification_quote: experiment.py comment 'fresh task instance each episode (fresh initial files)' and 'guarantee clean per-episode state' — framed for data cleanliness, not welfare.
